/* A DERIVATION STEP IS CENTRED, and has room.
   A maths answer is a chain of equalities — `A² = A·A = [..]`, then
   `= [..]`, then `= O` — and the chain only reads as one if each step sits
   on the column's centre line. Left-aligned against a rule it reads as a
   list of unrelated equations, which is how ours looked beside the
   reference. Scoped to .subj-maths: physics sets 490 display equations
   against a rule and its pagination is tested with them there. */
.subj-maths .dm { text-align:center; margin:11px 0; }

/* Side-by-side matrices are a step too, and centre with the rest. */
.subj-maths .mxrow { justify-content:center; margin:11px 0; }

/* A LONG EQUATION WRAPS. IT MUST NEVER BE CUT OFF.
   `.acol .dm` carries `overflow-x:hidden` (elements/acols) so a display
   equation cannot push a horizontal scrollbar into a two-column page. On
   screen that hides the overflow; on PAPER it deletes it, and nothing
   errors — the page's scrollHeight never grows, so step09's clip check and
   step15's overflow check both pass while the reader loses the end of the
   line.

   Measured on `physics_edited.md`'s 2025 associativity proof, whose RHS is
   one unbroken chain:
     RHS = {(hog) of}(x) = (hog)[f(x)] = h[g{f(x)}] = h[g(2x)]
           = h[3(2x)+4] = h(6x+4) = sin(6x+4)
   It ended at `sin(6x` on the page. The remaining `+4)` was simply gone.

   FORMAT_SPEC 8.2 already settles what to do, for the matrix case: let it
   WRAP at its own boundary, never shrink the font — a visibly smaller
   equation beside normal ones reads as a bug even when the shrink is
   consistent. Same answer here. `overflow-wrap:break-word` is the rule
   chemistry already uses on `.dm` for its wide reaction lines; this is
   that rule for maths, plus restoring `overflow-x` so nothing is clipped
   while it wraps.

   `max-width:100%` keeps the box inside the column so the wrap actually
   triggers, mirroring what `.subj-maths .mx` above does for a wide matrix. */
.subj-maths .dm, .subj-maths .acol .dm {
    overflow-x:visible; overflow-wrap:break-word; max-width:100%; }
